snippet.textDisplay:
Chamber of Secrets is unique in that it's a borderline horror movie. At least for kids and young adults.

The latter films are definitely darker in tone. But, nothing has come close to being as scary as the voices Harry hears during the basilisk sections. That combined with literally everyone being attacked and petrified really makes you feel like Harry and Ron are in way over their heads. 

Plus, Gilderoy Lockhart is just the goat Ravenclaw.

snippet.textDisplay: Chamber of secrets holds a special place in my heart because I was a massive fan on the first film as a kid and eagerly awaited the second film. My brother and I got the sticker book, collected newspaper clippings and magazine pages based on the upcoming COS. We recorded the trailers. When it came out, I remember making props like the howler, wands, chocolate frog cards. I even made a nimbus 2001. My brother I eye would run around the garden on the broomsticks I made, throwing a ball to each other and then trying to shoot it into a basket ball net. Such happy memories. I still have all the sticker books and drawings I did as a kid.

snippet.textDisplay:
I really like the Half Blood Prince movie! (I know Radcliffe doesn't because of his personal issues) Especially the vibe and music is great :D
Especially since the 4th focused more on the 3 tasks and the 5th felt quite rusked (longest book, shortest movie (DH2 is shorter, but yeah that's only half a book). 
So when it comes to HP 6, it finally got more teenage HP school vibes, from the earlier movies (at least to me). 
It was more about the characters themselves, schools stuff, Quidditch, of course more Draco scenes with the dark tone (who was pretty put to the minimum in the 4th and 5th movie).
Eventhough it's quite different from the book which was like 1/3 school stuff, 1/3 Voldy background, 1/3 Malfoy plotting things.  And here it was like 1/2 school stuff, and the other half Malfoy with a bit of little bit of Voldy. 
I still really liked it, and but the more voldy background, I was just okay with re-reading the book chapters (weren't really scenes I was looking forward to the most, so to say). Neither did I miss them when watching the movie.
